chunks: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ja'far ibn Ibrahim who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say,'
One who knows the appropriate position of his speech in relation to his intellect reduces his speech about that which does not concern him.

And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Beware of arguing with a deluded individual, for indeed every deluded individual has an argument that lasts only until his time comes to an end, and when his time is up, his delusion burns him with the Fire.'

key_terms.مَوْضِعُ كَلَامِهِ: the appropriate position/place of his speech
key_terms.مُفْتَنٍ: deluded individual / one tested by fitnah
key_terms.يَعْنِيهِ: concerns him / is relevant to him

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of knowing the 'position of speech' in relation to intellect according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links intellectual maturity directly to linguistic restraint, teaching that true wisdom lies in distinguishing between necessary speech and idle talk. The warning against 'al-muftan' (the deluded) reflects the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between sincere seekers and those consumed by temporary, superficial arguments, whose eventual defeat is a divine consequence of their own misguidance. This concept is deeply rooted in the tradition of *hikmah* (wisdom) as a filter for speech, ensuring that words serve truth rather than ego.
